releases.body:
First public release — published on npm as `magpie-plugin-msmoli@0.1.0`.

## What it does

A [magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie) plugin that claims ModelScope's
(魔搭) daily **魔粒** credits for you — one check-in a day instead of opening
the site — and shows the balance and today's spend on the account's usage card.

- **Daily check-in.** `GET /api/v1/users/login/info` is the claim trigger; the
  plugin reads the ledger, touches the endpoint, then reconciles against the
  ledger again, so "claimed 200" is what actually landed, not what was asked
  for. Idempotent within the day.
- **Check-in window.** Defaults to 08:30–10:00 Beijing time, configurable in
  `msmoli.json`; the end is capped at 23:00 so a retry still lands on the same
  day.
- **Usage card.** 魔粒 balance, today's earned/spent, and the countdown to when
  the day's grants expire (24 hours after they land).
- **Token sync CLI.** `npx magpie-plugin-msmoli` copies an existing ModelScope
  key between magpie's built-in preset and this plugin's sign-in, without ever
  printing the token.
- **No models registered.** Chat keeps using the built-in `modelscope` preset;
  this provider exists only to carry the sign-in the check-in runs as.

## Install

```bash
magpie plugin add magpie-plugin-msmoli
printf 'ms-your-token\n' | magpie plugin login msmoli
```

Or install from GitHub (`magpie plugin add github:MisonL/magpie-plugin-msmoli`)
or from a clone — all three are in the README.

## Notes

- Tests: 431 at this tag, run on Node (three clock modes) and Bun in CI across
  macOS, Windows and Linux.
- **Not listed in magpie's Discover list.** The registry PR
  ([plugins#714](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/pull/714)) was
  declined: ModelScope has no check-in endpoint, so the plugin makes the server
  count a website sign-in, and the market does not simulate rewards that are
  meant to require real activity. ModelScope's terms prohibit plugins that
  interfere with the service and "刷分", so use of this package is a risk taken
  on your own account. The project will not submit it to the market again;
  it stays installable by name from npm. The English README's
  "Purpose, responsibility, and risk" section states this in full.
